name: Williams Creek and Forgotten Falls
description:
Registration with the walk leader is essential. Information is below. 
Must be over 18yrs to participate.  

RATED 
Easy (6 hrs walking) - mostly on track walking.

These walks have been very popular, so register ASAP to reserve a spot. 

DESCRIPTION
This walk includes an old rainforest logging track, then a steep descent on bush track to Williams Creek and Platypus Pool (great swim). Then a track short climb over the hill to Forgotten Falls, which is lovely this time of year, and another swim. Then a short steep scrambly climb to top of the waterfall, then a track walk to the cars.

This is a bush track walk in remote area. Whilst a track walk, there is uneven footings e.g. tree roots, rocks, some creek crossings (wet rocks), steep slopes, and some scrambling around the falls. 
 
WHAT TO BRING
- Wear appropriate footwear, i.e., enclosed sturdy shoes. 
- Drinking water - carry 2 lt, refill from creeks as required (but suitably treat/filter any water refills from natural sources, or carry 4 to 5 lt). The club also recommends use of electrolytes during the day. 
- Bring food and snacks to suits your energy needs for full day bushwalking. 
- Bushwalkers should bring their own personal (minimal) first aid kit, headtorch, and whistle. The club does not provide a group first aid kit. 
- Hat is mandatory, sunscreen and insect repellent is recommended.
- Clothing- long sleeve clothing is recommended. 

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 8am at Paluma Village Community Centre
Return time: Back at cars at approx. 4-5pm

COST
Non-member walk fee of $5 

MORE INFO AND REGISTRATION
Walk leader is Wilfred. Please contact Wilfred via his mobile or send us an email at tsvbush@hotmail.com (we will forward phone numbers on).


**Please note:
To protect the privacy of club officials, walk leaders, property owners or sensitive areas, contact details and some locations won't be published on Facebook or website or be given out via private message. Please contact the club via email and we will respond ASAP.
On some activities, walker numbers may be limited to promote the safety and enjoyment of all, due to location size and ability to socially distance or to reduce our environmental impact at some locations.
COVID-19
Please do not attend if you are unwell, have symptoms or meet any conditions imposed as per Qld Government. Social distancing and self managed hygiene practices are strongly encouraged, and the club will not be organising car pooling opportunities at present. The club is cognisant of the Outdoors Queensland COVID SAFE PLAN for Outdoor Recreation Providers. On some walks, as noted above, numbers may be limited.
We hope to see you on a walk soon.

name: Little Birthday to Big Birthday, Mt Spec area
description:
Leader – Luen 

An off-track remote wilderness exploratory adventure.  

Continuing our recent theme of off-track wilderness creek-based exploring in the Mt Spec area, this Saturday we try Little Birthday Creek to Birthday Creek. 

Rated - Hard. 

These walks have been very popular, so register ASAP to reserve a spot. 

Must contact the walk leader to register and for full details prior to attending. 
To register contact Luen 0415947748 or luenwarneke@gmail.com 

Meet at 8am Paluma Village Community Centre car park, normal place. Then we drive to near Paluma Dam to start the adventure.

Full day hike, anticipate back at the cars around 4 to 5 pm.

This is a remote wilderness creek bushwalk. You may be walking in the water, rockhopping, there will be slippery rocks, uneven footing, slippery tree roots, tangled vines, maybe wait-awhile, leeches, all that good fun rainforest adventure. Gotta luv rainforest uh ! The rewards are great scenery, fun adventure, good laughs, a sense of achievement, and great company. See photos on the club's Facebook or Luen's website wanderstories.space for examples of potential bushwalking conditions from the recent similar creek based exploratory adventures. 
 
Wear appropriate footwear, i.e., enclosed sturdy shoes that grip on slippery rocks and that can handle walking in water. 

Drinking water - carry 2 lt, refill from creeks as required (but suitably treat/filter any water refills from natural sources, or carry 4 to 5 lt). The club also recommends use of electrolytes during the day. 

Bring food and snacks to suits your energy needs for full day bushwalking. 

Bushwalkers should bring their own personal (minimal) first aid kit, headtorch, and whistle. Luen will also have his personal minimal first aid kit. The club does not provide a group first aid kit. Hat is mandatory, sunscreen and insect repellent is recommended.

Fees: non-members $5 
 
Clothing- as it off-track bushwalking, long sleeve clothing or gaiters is recommended. Otherwise you may have cuts/scratches on exposed skin at the end of the day. 

Must be over 18yrs to participate.

name: Porcupine Gorge remote wilderness bushwalking
description:
leader Keith tsvbush@hotmail.com (limited numbers – only two spots open)  

A 32 km remote wilderness through walk (point to point) of Porcupine Gorge. No tracks, all true bushwalking with many creek crossings. Spectacular scenery and fantastic camping. A great adventure and one of our highlights of the year. Suitable for experienced multi-day remote area bushwalkers. Contact the leader for details.
